TextView.android:text: Sonar is an assistive vision system designed to help visually impaired users understand their surroundings through real-time object detection, proximity awareness and spoken feedback.
The prototype runs entirely on-device — no servers, no data leaves this phone.
Point your camera at the room around you. Sonar will identify objects, estimate distances and describe the scene aloud.
Press Start camera to begin. Detected objects will be outlined and described aloud.
Sonar translates visual information into spoken guidance — helping users navigate spaces, identify objects and read text independently.
Three parallel pipelines work together — turning visual input, spatial data and voice commands into meaningful audio guidance.
Navigating unfamiliar indoor spaces with confidence — knowing where doorways, stairs and furniture are located.
Locating personal belongings by asking the system to scan the room and report where common objects are.
Accessing printed information — bus numbers, street signs, product labels, menus — by pointing the camera and asking.
Receiving continuous updates about nearby people and open paths — making crowded environments less overwhelming.
“Three people ahead. Open path on your left.”
The proposed wearable uses established open-source components. This Android prototype substitutes equivalent on-device SDKs for the same pipeline.
Bone Conduction — audio without blocking ambience
Object detection — YOLOv8 on the wearable; ML Kit Object Detection in this app
Text reading — Tesseract OCR; ML Kit Text Recognition here
Voice — Whisper / Web Speech; Android SpeechRecognizer here
Speech output — gTTS / Festival; Android TextToSpeech here

Sonar is designed around local processing, reducing dependence on cloud connectivity and keeping sensitive environmental information close to the device. The camera feed, detection results and personal data are processed on the device itself — nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored externally.
This Android prototype demonstrates the same principle: once the app is installed, it runs entirely offline. No data leaves this phone.
These figures represent the expected performance described in the project proposal — targets for the fully developed system.
The project proposal identifies several directions for extending Sonar's capabilities beyond the initial prototype.
Adopting newer, more accurate detection architectures as they become available for edge deployment.
Moving beyond individual object labels to describe spatial relationships and scene context.
Replacing ultrasonic sensors with LiDAR or structured-light depth cameras for richer 3D data.
Adding location awareness and inertial measurement for outdoor navigation and route guidance.
Thermal sensors for heat sources, and vibration motors for non-audio directional alerts.
Extending speech synthesis and recognition to additional languages for broader accessibility.
Connecting with traffic signals, public transport systems and emergency services.
A phone app for remote monitoring, configuration and extending system reach.
Assistive technology for a more navigable world.
Student mini-project prototype · Built with CameraX, ML Kit & Android TextToSpeech · No data leaves this device.
